title: Drone-agnostic sensor-to-map TAK plugin (MISB KLV to georegistered footprints, incremental 3D Tiles and change-vs-baseline overlays on a commodity edge box) with bandwidth-budgeted delta distribution of terrain and basemap packages across TAK federations
problem: Small-unit and public-safety TAK users who fly commercial drones cannot, without cloud reach-back or a vendor-specific ground station, turn any MISB-KLV video feed into a georegistered footprint, a fresh 3D Tiles model and a change-vs-baseline alert on their own map, and cannot keep terrain and basemap packages current across federated TAK Servers over bandwidth-limited links.
echelons: TAK Server administrator (unit, agency or allied)

user.exact_role: Company/battalion small-UAS operator or S2 geospatial NCO (12Y) on ATAK; incident-management-team situation unit leader or drone-as-first-responder pilot on ATAK-CIV/iTAK; TAK Server administrator managing a federation
user.echelon: Company through brigade (Army/USMC/SOF); county/state incident management team (public safety); agency TAK Server admin (DHS/CBP, allied)
organization_examples: Army brigade S2 geospatial cells and company sUAS teams flying Skydio X10D / Parrot / Anduril Ghost-class MISB-emitting drones
USSOCOM teams (Reveal Farsight was developed with USSOCOM)
CAL FIRE and California incident management teams that reviewed helicopter video in ATAK (Caldor Fire)
DHS S&T TAK program users (wildland fire, CBP, FEMA)
Allied ATAK users (UK, NATO SOF, Australia) and German civil-protection agencies (public evidence on German TAK adoption insufficient)

current_workflow: Drone streams RTSP/H.264 with a MISB 0601 KLV track to the controller; the operator opens the stream in ATAK's video tool or the free government UAS Tool plugin, which draws the drone icon, sensor point of interest (SPI) and, when four-corner metadata is present, the video footprint on the map in real time.

For a 3D product, the operator either uses the drone vendor's onboard/controller modelling (Skydio Onboard Modeling produces a textured mesh on the controller within minutes), a vendor edge app (Reveal Farsight builds 2D/3D 'in moments' and exports tiles to ATAK), or uploads imagery post-flight to a cloud (DroneDeploy, Pix4D, Skydio Cloud, WebODM) and waits hours.
Change relative to the previous flight is judged by eye, side by side, or is not done at all; enterprise change detection (Vantor/BlackSky under NGA Luno) never reaches the edge device.

Basemaps and 3D terrain (MBTiles/GeoPackage, OWT/Cesium 3D Tiles) are pre-packaged by the geospatial cell or pulled with community tools (takwerx map-depot) and sideloaded by USB or pushed as TAK mission packages; refreshes during an operation are rare.
After a link outage, TAK Server mission sync and federation re-converge CoT and mission content; large packages saturate the link or are simply not re-sent.
current_solution: Government-owned free software (ATAK core video tool + TPC/PAR UAS Tool plugin + MediaMTX) for KLV footprint/SPI overlay; drone-vendor onboard modelling (Skydio X10/X10D) and vendor edge apps (Reveal Farsight, Edgybees Argus for georegistration) for 3D; cloud photogrammetry (DroneDeploy, Pix4D, DJI, WebODM/OpenDroneMap) when connectivity exists; TAK Server mission sync/federation, CloudTAK package sync, community map-depot plugin and AGC Releasable Basemap Tiles for map distribution; Ditto Edge Sync for overlay sync; manual sideloading otherwise.
failure: The remaining unmet slice is narrow: (1) no free or government-owned tool computes change-vs-baseline overlays from drone imagery on the edge device; (2) no drone-agnostic, vendor-neutral edge service turns any KLV feed into incremental 3D Tiles that TAK displays without a Skydio or Reveal licence; (3) no fielded service prioritises and delta-distributes 3D terrain and basemap packages across TAK federations under a bandwidth budget. The first item (live KLV footprint on the map) is already solved by free government software.

evidence.claim: The ATAK UAS Tool plugin (government-distributed, free) displays drone video in the map interface when four-corner metadata is present, shows a sensor point-of-interest (SPI) marker for the camera stare point as video plays, and overlays MIL-STD-2525 markers on the video; i.e., 'MISB KLV to georegistered footprint' is a stock capability of the government-owned ecosystem.
evidence.source_title: ATAK UAS Tool User Guide 10.0 (mirror) and Google Play listing 'ATAK Plugin: UAS Tool'
evidence.pub_date: not captured (manual v10.0; mirror at scribd.com/document/632077442)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Public-safety agencies are adopting a fully free stack (ATAK + UAS Tool + MediaMTX streaming server) for fire, law-enforcement and SAR drone operations; if the stream carries MISB/KLV metadata ATAK overlays what the camera sees in real time. This shows the public-safety buyer's revealed price point for the footprint feature is zero.
evidence.source_title: The Free Drone Tech Stack Changing Public Safety (HSToday)
evidence.pub_date: not captured (page fetch EGRESS_BLOCKED; claim from search summary)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Skydio X10/X10D Onboard Modeling generates a textured 3D mesh or 2D map on the controller within minutes after the flight, and X10D streams to the ATAK network offline or online; the Army selected X10D to replace the RQ-28A at company level. The 'incremental 3D on a commodity edge box' function is therefore a stock feature of the Army's chosen company-level drone rather than a gap.
evidence.source_title: Skydio: A new dimension for 3D scanning with Onboard Modeling; Skydio X10D Integrates with ATAK for Tactical ISR; support article 'Using ATAK UAS Tool plugin on a Third Party Controller with Skydio X10D'
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Reveal Technology's Farsight processes ISR feeds into 2D and 3D models 'in mere moments' on mobile hardware in comms-limited environments, imports/exports map tiles and data layers to ATAK, was developed with USSOCOM, and in May 2025 partnered with Maxar to integrate high-resolution basemaps and 3D data at the tactical edge; Reveal raised a $30M Series B with stated intent to acquire companies. The defense edge-3D-to-ATAK slot is occupied by a funded, acquisitive vendor.
evidence.source_title: Reveal and Maxar Partner to Enhance Farsight Platform Capabilities (PR Newswire); Reveal Raises $30M Series B (Tectonic Defense)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The TAK Product Center's TAK Offsite 2026 agenda includes an Army Geospatial Center 'Releasable Basemap Tiles Demonstration' and a 'Cesium Program Update: 3D Tiles', showing that native 3D Tiles support and government-authored basemap packaging are on the government-owned roadmap.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: AGC's Releasable Basemap Tiles program publishes its packaging work openly (agcgeoint/rbt on GitHub) and is validating a draft OGC 'Basemap Tile Packages' GeoPackage extension in an OGC sprint; the basemap-packaging layer a startup would build on is government-authored and in flux.
evidence.source_title: OGC GeoPackage Sprint | Releasable Basemap Tiles & VTIS Testing; GitHub agcgeoint/rbt
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: OpenDroneMap (stable 3.5.6, 2025-07-07) is an open-source photogrammetry toolkit producing maps and 3D models from drone imagery, and the Obj2Tiles tool converts OBJ output to OGC 3D Tiles; the core 'imagery to 3D Tiles' algorithms are open and free.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DHS S&T runs and is expanding the Team Awareness Kit for first responders; California IMT-4's situation unit reviewed helicopter video of the Caldor Fire in ATAK and DHS S&T evaluated WIFIRE Edge with local fire departments to feed UAS and sensor data into TAK. The public-safety TAK user base is real and the sponsor is DHS S&T, but the evidence describes a government program adding capability, not a procurement of a third-party plugin.
evidence.source_title: DHS S&T's Team Awareness Kit Expands Its Reach (HSToday / Team Orlando); UAS for Safety of Life in Southern California (Inside Unmanned Systems)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DHS S&T SAVER published a 'Drone as First Responder' TechNote (July 2025), indicating federal public-safety attention to DFR programs; no budget line for TAK sensor-to-map plugins is evidenced.
evidence.source_title: TechNote July 2025 SAVER-T-TN-50 Drone as First Responder (DHS S&T)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Commercial public-safety drone platforms already deliver drone position and live video into TAK: DroneSense markets a 'TAK Geospatial Interface', PAR Government documents the UAS Tool for telemetry/FMV/C2, and COTAK (Colorado's state TAK program) lists integrations; the public-safety sensor-to-map channel is already served.
evidence.source_title: Drone telemetry integration with TAK (Corvus Intel); PAR Government 'UAS Tool'; COTAK Integrations
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The Army buys UAS FMV improvements through SBIR topics (an Army SBIR topic 'Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Full Motion Video (FMV) Enhancement' exists in the closed-topic archive), and AFWERX has replaced propose-anything Open Topics with 'Focused Open Topics' after resuming solicitations in April 2026; the vehicle for this kind of feature is SBIR, which carries the U.S.-ownership test.
evidence.source_title: Army SBIR|STTR topic: UAS FMV Enhancement; AFWERX in 2026 (Grant Engine)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: PM Mission Command's Operational Mission Command Suite notice asks for DDIL-robust TAK data services, a data fabric and catalog - the only government requirement text touching the distribution half - but it is framed as a suite requirement for an integrator, not a plugin buy.
evidence.source_title: Operational Mission Command Suite (PM Mission Command notice), corpus finding E02-F8
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: TAK Server mission sync and federation, CloudTAK's package-sync endpoint, the community takwerx/map-depot plugin (elevation and basemaps into ATAK) and Ditto's mission-ready Edge Sync plugin already cover most of the 'delta distribution across federations' half; the G03 analysis found no bandwidth-budgeted priority scheduling of 3D terrain in the AGC/OGC material, which is the only residual.
evidence.source_title: Corpus: G03 evidence card and G03-score (TAK Server GitHub README fetched 2026-09-25; Ditto v1 release; CloudTAK GitHub)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: TAK is government-owned and free with 500,000+ users; the largest TAK services provider (PAR Government) was acquired by Booz Allen in 2024; the plugin ecosystem is TPC-approval-gated, has no licence revenue model and faces WinTAK-to-TAKX migration churn in 2026 - the economics of a TAK plugin business are services-shaped.
evidence.source_title: Corpus S07-G4 (tak.gov products; Breaking Defense 2025-11 TAK evolution article; Booz Allen TAK page)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: No public budget line names a drone-agnostic sensor-to-map plugin or bandwidth-budgeted geospatial distribution; Army money for edge exploitation flows through AIDP-Next (single-prime award expected Q1 FY2027) and TITAN production; DHS S&T TAK program funding detail is not public. Public evidence insufficient.
evidence.source_title: Corpus: G13 and G03 budget sections; Army FY2027 RDT&E BA 5D justification book (search summary only)
evidence.label: INFERENCE

evidence.claim: ATAK-CIV and its SDK are open-source government-owned software with a plugin architecture; TAK-GOV/MIL builds remain distribution-controlled - the unclassified MVP can be built without any government access, but military distribution goes through TPC.
evidence.label: FACT

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Because most of it is solved, just not by startups: the live KLV-to-footprint step is a free government plugin, on-drone 3D is a stock Skydio feature, edge 3D for SOF/Army is Reveal's product, native 3D Tiles and basemap packaging are on the TPC/AGC roadmap, and package/overlay sync is TAK Server, CloudTAK and Ditto. The pieces that remain (edge change-vs-baseline overlays, bandwidth-budgeted priority delta of 3D terrain across federations) are features whose users get the surrounding stack free, so no startup can charge enough to fund them, and the natural owners (TPC, AGC, Reveal, Skydio) can add them as increments. Vendor-neutrality is a disincentive for every drone maker and an indifference for the government, which already owns the neutral layer (TAK).
technical_wedge: If anything: an open-source ATAK-CIV plugin plus a headless Jetson/laptop service that (a) ingests any MISB 0601 KLV stream and stores keyframes with pose, (b) runs incremental OpenDroneMap-class reconstruction to 3D Tiles that ATAK/Cesium renders, (c) computes change-vs-baseline overlays (raster diff and mesh diff against the last flight or against USGS 3DEP/OWT-class baselines) with a tunable false-alarm threshold, and (d) exposes a content-addressed chunk manifest so a companion TAK Server plugin can delta-distribute 3D terrain and basemap packages mission-area-first under a per-link bandwidth budget. Items (c) and (d) are the only parts not already free or stock.

mvp.what: ATAK-CIV plugin + Jetson Orin edge service: any KLV drone feed -> footprint (existing), incremental 3D Tiles within ~5 minutes of landing, change-vs-baseline overlay with confidence, plus a TAK Server federation plugin that delta-syncs the resulting tiles and an AGC-format basemap package over a WAN-emulated 64 kbit/s link, mission-area-first.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes on open data and commercial hardware: two commercial drones (or recorded MISB sample streams), a Jetson Orin, two federated TAK Servers built from public source, a WAN emulator; approximately $60k-150k including one contracted photogrammetry engineer.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: Measured georegistration error against RTK ground truth; time-to-3D-Tiles per hectare on a Jetson; change-detection precision/recall on a staged scene (vehicles, berms, debris); bytes- and time-to-converge for terrain packages after an outage versus native TAK mission packages; and, decisively, that a real user (wildfire IMT, SAR team, or S2 cell) will choose it over the free ATAK/UAS Tool + Skydio/Reveal status quo and that some office will pay for it.

data_requirement.what: MISB 0601 KLV video with pose (drone-vendor streams or public sample files), drone still imagery for photogrammetry, baseline terrain and imagery (USGS 3DEP, Copernicus DEM, NAIP, OpenStreetMap, Cesium World Terrain), staged change scenes; no military FMV or OWT data needed for the MVP.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Yes; entirely open or self-collected. Military FMV, OWT/CUI data and TAK-GOV/MIL builds are sponsor-gated and would be needed only for a defense-validated demo.

entry_vehicle.primary: Open-source ATAK-CIV plugin release plus a TAK.gov / civTAK community listing to get users, then a paid pilot with one public-safety TAK program (state EM agency, COTAK-type) or an allied civil-protection user; defense entry only via xTech or an SBIR Direct-to-Phase-II once the cap table passes the U.S.-ownership test, or via subcontract/acquisition by Reveal, Skydio or a TAK services house.
sequence: Months 0-4: unclassified MVP on ATAK-CIV, Jetson, open data; publish plugin source

Months 3-6: five-to-ten user interviews (wildfire IMT, SAR, S2/12Y, TAK Server admins) and one TPC engineer conversation to confirm change-detection and priority delta-sync are not on the ATAK/TAK Server roadmap
Months 6-12: one paid public-safety or allied pilot; xTech entry; DHS S&T engagement
Months 12-24: SBIR D2P2 or DIU/other OT only if the ownership structure is resolved; otherwise partner or sell the team to Reveal/Skydio/a TAK integrator
entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires a small business more than 50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (13 CFR 121.702; armysbir.army.mil eligibility); the Indonesian founder's equity does not count and the German founder's counts only after permanent residency, so a naive 50/50 cap table fails (needs SBIR counsel). AFWERX limits foreign-national participation on awards to public-domain/fundamental research with work performed in the U.S. (AFRL-2025-3235 FAQ). DHS and allied civil-protection contracts and open-source distribution carry no SBIR ownership test but may involve FOCI-style or export review. TAK-GOV/MIL builds are distribution-controlled and would not be available to the non-U.S.-person founder without sponsor authorization. These are constraints to scope with counsel, not legal conclusions.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, but the relevant incumbents are smaller and closer: TPC can add change overlays and priority sync as ATAK/TAK Server releases (it already has the Cesium 3D Tiles program and AGC basemap packaging on its 2026 agenda); Reveal can add change-vs-baseline to Farsight and already exports to ATAK; Skydio can add change detection to Onboard Modeling; Ditto can extend Edge Sync to tile manifests. Each could do so in one or two release cycles (INFERENCE, MEDIUM). Anduril/Palantir do not need to respond because the government-owned free layer already occupies the vendor-neutral position.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Reject as a standalone company. The vendor-neutral, standards-based, free position that a startup would claim is already held by the government (TAK/UAS Tool/AGC/TPC), the drone-locked position by Skydio, and the paid defense edge-3D position by Reveal. The residual features have no requirement owner and a zero revealed price point among public-safety users. The only 'win' is speed to an open-source plugin that gets adopted and leads to an acqui-hire or a services relationship - a consultancy/acqui-hire path, not venture scale.

capital_required.credible_military_demo_usd: 600,000-1,500,000 (12-18 months: TAK-GOV/MIL access via a sponsor, exercise or soldier-touchpoint participation, TPC plugin review, a clearable U.S.-person field engineer) - INFERENCE from G03/G13 estimates scaled down for the narrower scope

capital_required.assumptions: Software-only, unclassified, commercial hardware; SBIR unavailable until the cap table is restructured; no licence revenue from military TAK users (government-owned ecosystem); figures are analyst estimates, not quotes.

expertise_required.role: Photogrammetry / SLAM / 3D-reconstruction engineer (incremental meshing, 3D Tiles, change detection)
expertise_required.why: The only non-commodity technical content is fast incremental reconstruction and low-false-alarm change detection on a Jetson; neither founder has it.

expertise_required.role: TAK ecosystem engineer with TPC relationships (ATAK/TAK Server plugin SDK, mission sync, federation, TAKX migration)
expertise_required.why: Plugin approval, release churn and knowing what TPC will ship next determine whether the product is obsoleted; relationships are the only early-warning system.

expertise_required.role: Public-safety or SOF domain seller who has run drone operations under TAK
expertise_required.why: The user must be convinced to pay for something adjacent to a free stack; a domain-credible seller is required for pilots.
Classification of the software (EAR99 vs 5D002/ENC vs USML XI if adapted for military sensors) and cap-table structure for SBIR must be settled before approaching DoD.

regulatory_burden.explanation: The unclassified ATAK-CIV/open-data product is likely commercial software (EAR99, or 5D002 with License Exception ENC if it ships encryption - RECALL, verify with counsel); no ATO is needed for public-safety pilots on agency-run TAK Servers, though state programs may require their own review. Burden rises to medium if the product is adapted for military sensors or distributed as a TAK-MIL plugin (TPC review; possible USML Category XI questions) and to high only if it were pulled into classified integration, which this scope excludes.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: In the unclassified public-safety form the Indonesian founder can participate fully in engineering. Constraints appear at the defense boundary: SBIR ownership/control test, AFWERX foreign-national limits, TAK-GOV/MIL distribution control, CUI/OWT data access, and any future facility clearance (FOCI review under 32 CFR 117). These need export-control, SBIR and DCSA counsel; no legal determination is made here.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Wildfire, SAR, disaster response, border and infrastructure-inspection users on TAK are real and offline-first has appeal; but the same users have shown they adopt free stacks (ATAK + UAS Tool + MediaMTX) and cloud mapping bundled with their drone platform (Skydio, DJI, DroneSense), so willingness to pay for a standalone plugin is unproven.

defensibility.explanation: Algorithms (ODM, Obj2Tiles, change detection) are open; interfaces (KLV, CoT, 3D Tiles, GeoPackage, TAK SDK) are open or government-controlled; data is open; there are no network effects in a plugin. The only accumulable assets are tuned change-detection thresholds from real flights, a deployed base of agency TAK Servers, and TPC/agency relationships - a head start, not a moat.

why_now: Since 2023: Jetson Orin-class edge compute makes minute-scale reconstruction feasible; the Army standardised on a KLV/CoT-emitting company-level drone (Skydio X10D) and DFR programs expanded drone flying in public safety; TPC is adding Cesium 3D Tiles to TAK and AGC is standardising basemap packages (2025-2026); OWT production (Vantor, Feb 2026) multiplies the 3D data that must reach edge devices; NGC2/DDIL requirements were written down. But the same changes let Skydio, Reveal and TPC ship the capability themselves, which they have.
killer_risk: The product's headline function (KLV to georegistered footprint) is already a free government plugin, its second function (minute-scale 3D on a commodity box) is a stock feature of the Army's chosen drone and the product of a funded, acquisitive competitor with ATAK export, and its third and fourth functions (edge change overlays, priority delta of terrain packages) are increments on roadmaps owned by TPC, AGC, Reveal and Ditto - with no requirement owner, no budget line and a public-safety buyer whose revealed price for the surrounding stack is zero. It is a feature set inside a government-owned, services-priced ecosystem, not a company.

allied_extension: Only marginally. Allied and coalition TAK users (UK, NATO SOF, Australia) and German civil-protection agencies sit outside NGC2 and could be a channel for the German founder, and allied civil users are less exposed to the SBIR ownership problem; but they inherit the same free ATAK/UAS Tool baseline, the same Skydio/Reveal/DJI alternatives, and TAK-MIL distribution control applies to them too. Public evidence on German or NATO civil TAK adoption at scale is insufficient. The allied angle changes the sales channel, not the feature-versus-company problem.
